description.narrative:
The use of Artificial Intelligence for surveillance, profiling and stifling activism is on the rise, creating a distressingenvironment that deepens existing inequalities, threatens activists, and silences dissent. This trend not onlyundermines the rightsof individuals but also stifles the voices of those fighting for change. With the rise of the farright exploiting digital tools for harm, It’s vital to recognize the implications for freedom and democracy, includingpublic discourse, especially during elections, shed light on the need for vigilance and action in defence of civilliberties. This project will empower 36 activists in the Netherlands and Spain to understand, expose, and counterthe systemic harms that artificial intelligence (AI) poses to activism and civic space. We willachieve this throughapplied research, cross-border learning exchanges, and the co-creation of activist-led strategic, replicablesolutions that enhance the resilience of activists against the weaponization of AI. The project will apply thefeminist influencing basket of resources and e-motive learning methodology that will engage the activists througha research aided context analysis and solution finding. It also builds a track record for ONL’s Dutch andEuropean programming on digital rights
Artificial Intelligence is a growing intersectional threat fueling climate misinformation, exacerbating harm inhumanitarian settings, targets vulnerable communities like LGBTQ, colored, black, Muslim, migrants, refugees,and aids manipulation in discourse and elections. The project aligns with Oxfam Novib and Intermon’s agendasto strengthen civic space and Dutch/European programming with a digital rights lens. By enabling andcollaborating with activists, it promotes transnational cooperation and innovative cross-border strategies. It pavesthe way for AI and environmental justice initiatives(CJ), enhances digital resilience in conflict zones (SAFE), andintegrates a feminist and genderperspective(ER4A). The project enhances ONL's visibilityon civic space anddigital rights while complementing existing efforts through Activist Lab, feminist resources, AACJ, Masarouna,and Tipping Point. It will also utilize Power to Voices, as a safer platform for activists, to further organize
The feminist influencing basket of resources and the emotive learning methodology, foster deep, intentionalcollaboration across Civic Space, ER4A, SAFE, CJ, Engagement, and LINK Units while linking with OxfamIntermon. In Q1, we work together to map threats, identifyactivists and commission a research. In Q2, we divedeeper in contextual analysis, bringing unitsand activists together to unpack activism amidst AI threats and startco-creating solutions. In Q3, we undertake matchmaking, to create transnational learninggroups, identify bestpractices and prepare a tailored program for exchange together with all units. Q4 brings all stakeholders togetherfor an exchange learning, production and dissemination of the research report and position paper featuring co-created solutions/recommendations. Continued exchange will be hosted on Power to Voices platform. Thisproject will also draw on experiences and synergies from AACJ, and Tipping Point projects to enrich outcomesand outreach.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib was founded in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Oxfam Novib is member of the Oxfam International confederation. Working together in the confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novib's main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. Oxfam Novib’s the Hague office contributes towards this project’s implementation.
